title: Media Queries
definition: A CSS technique introduced in CSS3 that allows content rendering to adapt to different conditions such as screen resolution, device width, or orientation.
simpleExplanation: An 'IF statement' for CSS. You can tell the browser: 'If the screen is smaller than 600px (like an iPhone), change the background to Red and make the font smaller. Otherwise, leave it alone.'
realWorldExample: Turning a 3-column desktop layout into a single-column layout on mobile devices so the user doesn't have to horizontally scroll.
useCases: Print styling (hiding navbars when printing a page)

basic: What symbol starts a media query?

answers.question: What does max-width mean?
answers.answer: It means 'Apply these styles ONLY if the screen width is 768 pixels or LESS'. If the screen is 800px wide, the rules inside the query are completely ignored.
